headline: Nikita Kucherov passes Steven Stamkos to become Lightning's career points leader
take:
ESPN reports that Nikita Kucherov became the Lightning's career points leader with an assist in the first period against the Utah Mammoth, passing Steven Stamkos. Daily Faceoff posted the same news: "Nikita Kucherov sets Lightning team scoring record."

The numbers say the record holder is playing like it. Kucherov has 13 points in 10 games so far this season, with 4 goals against 3.33 expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances), so his scoring is only a little ahead of his chances. At five-on-five, TBL has 64 percent of the expected goals when he's on the ice, and the team is 9 percentage points better with him out there. Tampa sits at 7-3-0 with 57 percent of the expected goals overall, though it is 2.8 goals short of what its chances suggested, so the record may be better than the results show. Stamkos, now in Nashville, has 10 points in 9 games so far this season, but NSH controls only 42 percent of five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice.
